title: First round of WNBA playoffs hit record viewership, Fever-Aces series hike numbers
content:
The WNBA announced Tuesday that the first round of the playoffs was the most-watched yet, with an average of 1.3 million viewers tuning in across networks over 10 games.

The three-game series between the Indiana Fever and Las Vegas Aces generated significant traffic. Even with a Thursday Night Football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns airing during the same window, the WNBA announced that Game 3 averaged 2.25 million viewers across USA Network and CNBC, becoming the most-watched WNBA first-round game ever and the most-watched playoff game since 2024.

Viewership during the win-or-go-home Game 3 peaked at 2.7 million. Only the Fever’s Game 2 loss in a sweep by the Connecticut Sun in Caitlin Clark’s rookie season had more viewers for a first-round game, with a record 2.5 million average.

This season’s playoffs are on track to break previous playoff viewership records. Over 11 first-round games in 2024, networks averaged 944 thousand viewers, 37 percent fewer than in 2025. This year’s first round has already broken 2024’s all-playoff viewership records when 1.1 million tuned in across 8 postseason games on ESPN and ABC.

This story will be updated.
